data.short_description: Sip & Forage is a new food cart pod from developers Tim Weiskind and Steve Master of Master Development, set to open in August at 1900 SW 5th Ave in downtown Portland near Portland State University. The project will bring up to 20 food carts to a 20,000-square-foot lot, alongside covered outdoor seating, a full bar cart, and natural gas hookups. The anchor will be Extra Credit, a bar concept housed inside an old bank building on the property.

Sofi'z Kitchen & Bar is relocating to 800 Bruce Road, Suite 100 in Chico, next to Bellachino's, with owner Sophia Ahmed announcing the move will occur during August. The new location will feature brand-new air conditioning, plenty of parking, and a space designed to handle the demands of a growing restaurant. The move comes after four years of challenges including air conditioning and plumbing issues at an older downtown building.

Babcia Bread, a Portland bakery known for pop-ups, is opening a permanent location at 10909 SE Main St in downtown Milwaukie, inside the historic Perry's Pharmacy Building. Co-founders Tommy Celt and Jade Novarino are behind the concept, which has received acclaim from Portland Monthly for its pastries. The location will place Babcia alongside fellow newcomers Sadie's on Main and Salon Fernweh inside the building.

data.short_description: Breadie's Cafe is set to open inside One City Church at 120 N East Yates Road in Memphis, with the main restaurant planned for autumn 2026 and an open porch set to open in spring 2027. The cafe, opened by Chris and Karin Conlee, will seat approximately 80 customers indoors and an additional 70 on the porch, along with a private dining room for events. The concept is described as a community-focused dining hub built around warmth, excellent food, and an inviting environment.

data.location: 2801 Windy Ridge Pkwy SE, Suite 100, Atlanta, GA 30339

The concept will offer diverse baking classes and dedicate approximately 1,000 square feet to a bakery serving baked goods and coffee, open Wednesday through Sunday. Quillin is partnering with Founders Row, an Atlanta-based brand incubator led by Jamie Weeks, to bring the concept to life.

Alice on the Avenue, a new neighborhood bar and gathering spot, is opening on August 8 at 1416 SE Morrison Street in Portland. The concept features an indoor garden aesthetic with shared plates, a full bar, and an all-ages atmosphere, alongside a whimsical cocktail list nodding to Alice in Wonderland. Owner Sheila Baraga brings nearly three decades of experience building neighborhood spots in Portland, making this her seventh business.

Dave's Hot Chicken is set to open a new location in Peabody's Northshore Mall at 210 Andover Street, slated to debut in mid-August 2026 on the Promenade next to Amigo's Mexican Kitchen & Tequila Bar. The Nashville-style hot chicken chain lets guests choose spice levels ranging from "No Spice" to the infamous "Reaper," which requires customers to sign a waiver. This will be the franchisee Almerindo Graziano's location as part of an agreement to develop 10 Dave's Hot Chicken restaurants throughout the northwest Boston region.

Mary Brown's Chicken opened its flagship restaurant at The Tenor in downtown Toronto on June 23, replacing Blaze Pizza after about 10 years at the location. The flagship uses new ordering formats and digital tools tested at other Toronto locations. Founded in Newfoundland in 1969, Mary Brown's recently celebrated reaching 300 Canadian locations.

Customers can expect the chain's signature hand-breaded chicken, sandwiches, combos, snacks, and sides made with Canadian ingredients.

The Get Down Lounge is coming to 1429 SE 37th Ave in Portland's Hawthorne neighborhood, with owners Jake and Shela Kagan targeting a mid-August opening in the former 3 Doors Down restaurant space. The roughly 2,400-square-foot spot will feature big booths, greenery, a DJ booth spinning Motown and blues, a large screen showing Soul Train, and outdoor seating with a capacity of approximately 60 people. The Kagans recently moved from San Francisco and are funding the project themselves with no outside investors.

data.short_description: Game Day Social is a sports bar and tavern under construction at 6919 Orchard Lake Road in West Bloomfield Township, Michigan. Owner Brandon Bahoura has not yet set a firm opening date but expects to open sometime in August. The menu features pub-style food, craft cocktails, and chef-driven dishes including grilled salmon, burgers, and crispy chicken sandwiches.

data.status: plans to open in late July
data.short_description: Oh Yea Pizza is a pizzeria opening in Aiken, South Carolina, serving classic and specialty pizzas, strombolis, calzones, subs, an all-you-can-eat salad bar, and crispy wings. The shop's tagline is "We knead dough, you need pizza" and it will offer gluten-free and keto-friendly cauliflower crust options. Grand opening promotions and giveaways are scheduled for the late July opening.

D-Spot Dessert Café is opening its first U.S. location in Carrollton, Texas, marking the Canadian chain's debut in the American market. The café offers a menu of Belgian waffles, crepes, cheesecakes, handmade ice cream, milkshakes, burgers, sandwiches, and pasta. The grand opening on July 11 will feature BOGO promotions, free face painting, balloon art, and a $1,000 gift card giveaway.

data.status: will close at the end of July
data.short_description: Gris-Gris, an award-winning New Orleans restaurant on Magazine Street, announced its closure at the end of July after eight years of operation. Owner and chef Eric Cook cited it as a business decision, with the announcement shared on Instagram. For its final month, the restaurant is reviving its original 2018 menu at 2018 prices.

data.status: recently opened (soft opening); grand opening on August 3
data.short_description: Nan Xiang Soup Dumplings, a New York-based Michelin Guide-recommended soup dumpling brand, opened its first Georgia location on July 3 in Buford. The restaurant serves handmade Shanghai-style soup dumplings, pan-fried pork buns, Shanghai-style noodles, and other regional specialties. A grand opening celebration is scheduled for August 3.

data.status: opening its doors this Friday, July 10
data.short_description: Takay is a new 10-seat Japanese omakase restaurant opening in Miami's Coral Way on July 10, founded by Glen Kotlyarski and Yoni Matz. The 800-square-foot space features traditional Japanese design elements including a Zen garden entrance and a hinoki wood installation inspired by Hokusai's The Great Wave. It will offer a 17-course Edomae-style omakase menu priced at $250 per person, with two nightly seatings at 6 p.m. and 9 p.m.

data.status: plans to open its doors as early as late August or early September 2026
data.short_description: Buffalo Wild Wings is opening its first Kyle, Texas location at 1080 Kohlers Crossing, operated as a family-owned franchise by DLK Foods. The roughly 5,500-square-foot restaurant is part of a broader Austin-area expansion by franchisee Donald Semien's group. The menu will feature wings, sandwiches, wraps, and salads alongside a full bar and multiple televisions for sports viewing.

Juanis Restaurant, a Dallas-area Mexican restaurant known for homestyle cooking and a made-to-order menu, is opening a new standalone location at 10830 Harry Hines Blvd within the Grand Bazaar development. Owner Juana Aguirre built the brand from a small taqueria inside a gas station over the past decade and has since closed her previous location at 10817 Denton Dr. The new location will operate fully independently with no outside administration.

data.location: 1397 N Highland Ave NE, Atlanta, GA 30306
data.short_description: Alere is a new neighborhood restaurant concept from the team behind The Chastain, led by Chef Christopher Grossman, planned for Morningside Village in Atlanta. The seasonal menu will draw from Southern European cuisine with locally sourced ingredients and classical cooking techniques. The project is still in early conceptual development, with further details and a more specific timeline to be announced closer to opening.

data.location: 603 N La Cienega Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90069
data.status: hope to open in about a month
data.short_description: The One Rooftop is a new 16,000-square-foot rooftop bar and restaurant taking over the former E.P. & L.P. space in West Hollywood. The venue will feature a rooftop lounge, outdoor bar, indoor restaurant space, and rooftop greenspace with views of the Hollywood Hills. It is designed to host pop-up restaurants, seasonal residencies, corporate events, film production, and private celebrations.

data.location: 7501 W Cermak Rd, North Riverside, IL 60546
data.status: opening date has not yet been announced; timeline for construction is still being evaluated
data.short_description: 7 Brew is confirmed to be opening a new location at North Riverside Park Mall at 7501 W Cermak Road in North Riverside, Illinois. The franchise operator is Who Brew, which has been expanding 7 Brew locations across Chicagoland. The menu includes hot and cold brew coffees, energy drinks, fizz drinks, teas, lemonades, and shakes.

Don Ladis Taco Shop, a San Diego-style Mexican restaurant originally located in Gresham, Oregon, is opening a second location in Damascus at 19850 SE Hwy 212. Owner Sonia Lopez confirmed the expected August opening for the family-run restaurant. The menu features carne asada burritos, breakfast tacos, rolled tacos, shrimp tacos, al pastor, and weekend menudo, with a salsa bar as a standout feature.

Mazzio's Pizza and Wings in Kilgore, Texas permanently closed on July 3, 2026 after 41 years in business. The restaurant team shared the closure news on Facebook, thanking the community for four decades of support, though no specific reason for the closure was provided. The location served pizza, wings, and Italian-American favorites and was a longtime community gathering spot.

Ship Lantern Inn, a century-old fine dining restaurant in Milton, New York, has permanently closed after more than 100 years of service in the Hudson Valley. Owner Mike Foglia, a third-generation family member, cited the lack of a family successor as the reason for closure, noting the decision was not financially motivated. The Foglia family opened the restaurant in 1925 and Foglia has expressed hope to find a new owner for the historic property.

Paris Bistro, a French restaurant in downtown Naperville, permanently closed on June 7, 2026 after 13 years of operation. The restaurant announced the closure on social media, thanking guests for their years of support. It was known for its classic French cuisine, intimate dining atmosphere, and weekend brunch service.

Wahlburgers closed its St. Charles, Illinois restaurant on June 29, 2026, marking the end of the brand's presence in Illinois. Founded by brothers Mark, Donnie, and Chef Paul Wahlberg, the chain is known for burgers, sandwiches, loaded fries, and shakes. The company stated it plans to open a new location in the future, though no additional details were announced.

Nona's Italian Grill, a longtime favorite in The Woodlands, Texas, permanently closed on June 1, 2026 after nine years in business. Founded by Juan Garcia, the restaurant was known for its Northern Italian cuisine, homemade pasta, and welcoming atmosphere, and had expanded to a second location in the Woodforest area of Montgomery.

data.location: Garden Oaks / The Stomping Grounds, Houston, TX (Address not specified)
data.short_description: Pho Fix, located at The Stomping Grounds in Garden Oaks, Houston, permanently closed on June 8, 2026 after five years of operation. The restaurant was known for traditional Vietnamese dishes including slow-simmered pho, vermicelli bowls, and banh mi sandwiches, with a menu inspired by owner Danny Pham's family recipes.

data.location: T.C. Jester Boulevard, Houston, TX (Address not specified)
data.status: announced its closure on social media on June 25
data.short_description: Juanita's Mexican Restaurant on T.C. Jester Boulevard in Houston announced its closure on social media on June 25, 2026, after 25 years of serving the community. The family-owned Tex-Mex restaurant was a longtime neighborhood fixture.

Huey Magoo's is opening a new restaurant in Hialeah, Florida, marking its 90th location nationwide, with a grand opening ribbon-cutting ceremony on July 11 at 11 a.m. The chain is known for its hand-breaded chicken tenders marinated for 24 hours, and the menu also includes sandwiches, wraps, salads, and family meals. Grand opening promotions include a BOGO tender meal deal valid July 11–15 and a "Free Chicken for a Year" giveaway.

Piccolo Ristorante, a family-owned Italian restaurant in Bellmore, NY, permanently closed after a 47-year run. The restaurant served its final meal on July 3, 2026, with the closure announced on Facebook by owner Tom Valenti Jr. The post cited a "myriad of reasons" for the closure without providing specifics.

data.status: opening at some point in August
data.short_description: Wonder, a fast-casual food hall concept, is preparing to open a new location in Woodbridge, VA at Smoketown Station. The company website indicates the location will be customer ready at some point in August, though a precise opening date is not yet available. Wonder partners with high-profile chefs to recreate their signature concepts, with guests able to order from multiple restaurants on one bill.

Lindsey's Sandwich Shop is set to open in the Short Pump storefront previously occupied by Frostings Bake Shop at 4336 Pouncey Tract Road. Both concepts come from Lindsey Food Group, founded by Mike Lindsey and Kim Love-Lindsey. The new deli will serve lunch and dinner, featuring subs, hoagies, focaccia sandwiches, and paninis, with potential breakfast options in the future.

Frostings Bake Shop, a sweet treats storefront at 4336 Pouncey Tract Road in Short Pump, has closed and will be replaced by Lindsey's Sandwich Shop. Both the outgoing and incoming concepts are from the same ownership group, Lindsey Food Group. No specific closing date was mentioned in the article.

data.status: opening timeline not yet available; signage permits suggest customer ready by early 2027
data.short_description: Denver-based STK Steakhouse will be taking over the vacant space at 1 E. Pratt Street in Baltimore's Inner Harbor, previously occupied by Kona Grill. A definitive opening timeline is not yet available, but city permits indicate the restaurant hopes to have signage installed before end of 2026, suggesting an early 2027 opening. STK blends a modern steakhouse concept with a chic lounge for a fine dining experience.

Kona Grill ceased operations at 1 E. Pratt Street in Baltimore's Inner Harbor last winter, leaving the space vacant until STK Steakhouse takes over. Both Kona Grill and STK Steakhouse are owned by The One Group. No specific closing date was provided in the article.
